title: Resilient Microservices in Java: Spring Boot, Resilience4j and the Outbox
concept: Keep Rice Rocket's Java services up when their dependencies are not: timeouts and retry budgets, Resilience4j circuit breakers and bulkheads, idempotency keys, the transactional outbox, saga compensations, cache stampede protection and W3C trace context. Every lesson shows the Spring Boot configuration; the challenges are plain Java 21 graded in the code runner.
description: Keep Rice Rocket's Java services up when their dependencies are not: timeouts and retry budgets, Resilience4j circuit breakers and bulkheads, idempotency keys, the transactional outbox, saga compensations, cache stampede protection and W3C trace context. Every lesson shows the Spring Boot configuration; the challenges are plain Java 21 graded in the code runner. 8 lessons on one project, each applying the tool to a real production situation, with 1-2 graded challenges per lesson.

learningOutcomes.text: Set timeouts and retry budgets that do not multiply load during an outage.
Contain a failing dependency with circuit breakers and bulkheads.
Keep data consistent across services with idempotency keys, the outbox and sagas.
Protect caches from stampedes and follow one request across services with trace context.

knownIssues: Challenges are plain Java models of the documented Resilience4j and Spring behaviour, run in the code runner without the libraries.
